source.title: New results and open problems on Toeplitz operators in Bergman spaces

accepted.question_text: On the unit disk D, let A^p denote the Bergman space of analytic functions in L^p(D), and let T_a f = P(af) be the Toeplitz operator induced by a symbol a via the Bergman projection P. Find a sufficient and necessary condition for T_a to be bounded on A^p when the symbol is allowed to be merely L^1, locally integrable, or even distributional. In particular, for locally integrable symbols a, is the weighted-Sobolev condition a in W^{-m,∞}_ν(D) from equation (2.10) also necessary for boundedness of T_a : A^p -> A^p when 1 < p < ∞, at least in the Hilbert case p = 2?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Find a sufficient and necessary condition for Toeplitz operators with L1, or L1loc, or distributional symbols to be bounded on Bergman spaces Ap (for 1 < p < ∞ or at least for p = 2). Notice that for locally integrable and thus for L1-symbols, the condition (2.10) makes very well sense, and in view of Proposition 7 it is to be expected that (2.10) is weaker than (2.4). We in particular ask, if (2.10) is also a necessary condition for the boundedness of Ta : Ap → Ap, 1 < p < ∞, say, for a ∈ L1.

accepted.question_text: For Toeplitz operators on Bergman spaces of the unit disk with radial symbols, the paper discusses boundedness, compactness, and Fredholmness on A^2. Extend those radial-symbol results from the Hilbert Bergman space A^2 to the more general Bergman spaces A^p with 1 < p < ∞.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Generalize the results on boundedness, compactness and Fredholmness of Toeplitz operators on A2 with radial symbols to other Bergman spaces Ap.

accepted.question_text: On the unit disk D, with A^p the Bergman space and T_a the Toeplitz operator generated by a symbol a, find a necessary and sufficient condition for compactness of T_a on A^p when the symbol is only locally integrable, or even distributional. The paper asks for such a criterion at least in the Hilbert case p = 2.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Find a necessary and sufficient condition for Toeplitz operators with L1loc (or even distributional) symbols to be compact on Bergman spaces Ap (at least in the case p = 2).

accepted.question_text: Zorboska proved a compactness result for Toeplitz operators on A^2 under hypotheses involving the Berezin transform and the condition (3.1). Generalize that compactness theorem from A^2 to the other Bergman spaces A^p on the unit disk.

evidence.quote: She also posed a question of whether this result remains true when (3.1) holds for some p > 2.
Problem 4. Generalize Zorboska’s result on compactness to other Bergman spaces Ap.

accepted.question_text: Let T_a act on the Bergman space A^p of the unit disk, where the symbol a is matrix-valued. Find an index formula for Fredholm Toeplitz operators whose symbols lie in C(D) + H^∞(D), meaning sums of continuous matrix-valued functions on the closed disk and bounded analytic matrix-valued functions on the disk. The paper asks for this at least when p = 2, and also asks for the analogous index problem when the matrix-valued symbols belong to the Zhu class L^∞ ∩ VMO.

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Find an index formula for Fredholm Toeplitz operators on Ap with matrix-valued symbols in C(D) + H∞(D) (at least in the case p = 2). Also consider the index when the symbols are matrix-valued in the Zhu class L∞ ∩ V MO.

accepted.question_text: Extend the Fredholm theory for Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space A^2 with piecewise continuous symbols to the general Bergman spaces A^p on the unit disk. The paper also asks for the corresponding theory when the piecewise continuous symbols are matrix-valued.
accepted.context_brief: Fredholm theory for piecewise continuous symbols

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Extend Fredholm theory of Toeplitz operators on A2 with piecewise continuous symbols to other Bergman spaces Ap. Also consider matrix-valued piecewise continuous symbols.

accepted.question_text: Determine exactly when Hankel operators are bounded and when they are compact on L^1 in the Bergman-space setting, so that one can extend the Fredholm theory of Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space A^1.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Determine when Hankel operators are bounded and compact on L1, in order to extend Fredholm theory of Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space A1.

accepted.question_text: Let a be a distributional symbol in the weighted Sobolev class W^{-m,∞}_ν, and suppose its Berezin transform ṽa(z) tends to 0 as |z| -> 1. Must a then admit a representation a = ∑_{α \le m} (-1)^{|α|} D^α b_α in which each coefficient satisfies ess lim_{r->1} sup_{r<|z|<1} |b_α(z)| ν(z)^{-|α|} = 0? The paper notes that a positive answer would imply compactness of T_a on A^p and hence provide a necessary-and-sufficient compactness criterion.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Assume that a ∈ W−m,∞ν with ṽa(z) → 0 as |z| → 1. Find out whether the function a can then be represented in the following form (6.1) a = ∑α≤m (−1)|α|Dαbα, where ess lim r→1 sup r<|z|<1 |bα(z)|ν−|α|(z) = 0. An affirmative answer implies that Ta is compact on Ap, and hence provides a sufficient and necessary condition for Ta to be compact.

accepted.question_text: Let a be a distributional symbol in W^{-m,∞}_ν that already has a representation a = ∑_{α \le m} (-1)^{|α|} D^α b_α with each weighted coefficient b_α ν^{-|α|} continuous on the disk. Does it then follow that the Berezin transform ṽa is continuous on the disk? The paper states that a positive answer would help develop Fredholm theory for Toeplitz operators with distributional symbols.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. If a ∈ W−m,∞ν is of the form (6.1) with bαν−|α| ∈ C(D), does if follow that ṽa ∈ C(D)? A positive answer would be useful in the study of Fredholm properties of Toeplitz operators with distributional symbols.
